requirements.evidence: Contract matches: enum app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-14 with exact backing values; NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7); invokable action with exact signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:25). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB inside the transaction (:29-36). Ordering priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc (:95-97); mode filters priority > 0 / = 0 (:93-94). Fairness only in Any mode, last 3 by called_at desc, id desc, all priority (:42, :104-116), falling back to full ordering when no normal is claimable (:46). Candidate row locked and re-checked as waiting, skipped otherwise (:69-79). Only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set and model returned (:52-57). Exceptions thrown inside the transaction so nothing changes. Both docs updated. Small caveat: the streak history only counts tickets whose status is still 'called' (:108).

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php, a single invokable use-case class with no service layer; reuses InactiveQueueException; PHPDoc on the public method; docs/business-rules.md and docs/architecture.md ('Call the next ticket') updated; CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] (CHANGELOG.md:9). Authorization is omitted inside the action, but the task explicitly scopes it out and the doc records that (docs/business-rules.md:132).

security.evidence: No HTTP/Livewire surface. The task states the caller is trusted. Queue state is read from the DB under lockForUpdate rather than from the possibly stale model. No mass assignment: attributes are set explicitly (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:52-55). Exactly-once is guarded by the queue lock plus the candidate-row lock and re-check.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers: happy path with persisted fields (:39-56), write-once fields unchanged (:58-69), priority ordering (:71-81), issued_at/id tie-break (:83-94), other-queue isolation (:96-106), already-called never recalled (:108-119), priority_only and normal_only including empty-mode exceptions (:121-154), empty queue (:156-163), inactive queue using a stale instance (:165-176), fairness trigger, resume, two-streak, no-normal-waiting, priority_only counting toward the streak, normal reset, and modes ignoring fairness (:178-276), and a simulated concurrent Ticket::call() race (:278-304). Livewire auth/tamper tests are not applicable.

simplicity.evidence: About 117 lines. The fairness restriction reuses the same claim() with CallMode::NormalOnly instead of a separate query path (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:42-46). There are no extra abstractions beyond three small private helpers.

readability.evidence: Small, well-named methods (claim, nextCandidate, priorityStreakIsFull), a named constant PRIORITY_STREAK_LIMIT, and comments that explain the non-obvious skip list (:75-77). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only the action, the enum, the exception, its test, the two required docs and the CHANGELOG. No HTTP/Livewire or unrelated refactors. The edit to the Ticket::call() note in business-rules.md:102 is directly related.

issues.explanation: The fairness history filters on status = Called rather than called_at IS NOT NULL. If tickets later move to another status (served, finished), they drop out of the 'last 3 called' window and the streak may be computed wrongly.
The global Pest helper functions makeWaiting/makeCalled are declared in the file's global namespace and could collide with same-named helpers in other test files.
The race test triggers on any SQL containing 'issued_at', which is brittle if the query shape changes. It also runs on a single connection, so it does not exercise real row locks.
The doc states the queue-row lock serializes call-next with issuance and deactivation. That depends on IssueTicket and the deactivation path also locking the queue, which this diff does not show.

review.summary: Adds CallNextTicket with a CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException. It implements deterministic ordering, the three modes, the 3-priority fairness rule, the inactive-queue check read under a queue-row lock, and exactly-once selection with a candidate lock and re-check. Thorough Pest tests and the required doc/CHANGELOG updates are included. Only small nits remain, most notably that the fairness history counts only tickets whose status is still 'called'.
